p: Charge-off provides an accounting write-off option for delinquent loans while the loan portfolio remains active. The loan stays active and due for collection at the portfolio level, but is considered frozen, meaning no further transactions are expected though they can still occur and the loan does not close.
A charge-off transaction posts accounting entries when a loan is marked as charge-off.
Charge-off transaction entries:

tr.td: Income from ChargeOff Fees / Penalty Receivable

p: UNDO charge-off transaction entries:

tr.td: Fees Receivable / Income from ChargeOff Fees
Penalty Receivable / Income from ChargeOff Penalties
Loan Portfolio / Income from ChargeOff Fees

p: Charge-off accounting entries use new GL mapping fields in the loan product. Each field maps a charge-off amount to a general ledger account and type. Mapping is optional.

A charge-off transaction records the loan balance as a charge-off amount without changing the loan balance. Charge-off is triggered by non-payment of the remaining balance and is an accounting treatment, so it does not change data returned by existing APIs.
Charge-off amount rules:

ul.li: The charge-off amount equals the loan balance as of the charge-off date.
The charge-off amount is non-editable and auto-calculated.
A new dummy charge-off transaction is created for the charge-off amount.

p: You can backdate a charge-off transaction, but not before the last transaction date. You cannot set a charge-off date in the future.
Charge-off reason code rules:

ul.li: You can configure multiple charge-off rules.
You cannot configure the same reason code twice.

p: All actions, calculations, and transactions work normally as for a non-charge-off loan account. CHARGED_OFF status is never removed, even if the loan is PAID_OFF.

Interest accrual stops on a charge-off loan account, and no further discount amortization happens after charge-off. Every process that recalculates interest checks the charge-off date and performs no interest calculation beyond it. If the charge-off status is reversed, accrual resumes from the date it was previously stopped, and the final amortization transaction and its accounting entries are undone.

You can post all transaction types on a charge-off marked loan, and the accounting entries differ from those before charge-off. Chargeback, refunds, and other special case transactions are allowed, and the system does not restrict any transactions against the loan.
You cannot add charges after charge-off.

ul.li: Adding charges after charge-off is not allowed.

p: You can add or reverse a transaction dated before the charge-off date. The system applies standard accounting JE rules, then reverses and replays the charge-off transaction so the charge-off amount increases or decreases based on the reversal or new posting. If a backdated transaction fully pays the loan, the system reverses the charge-off transaction and lifts the charge-off flag.
Restrictions:

ul.li: Reversing a transaction that happened before or on the charge-off date is not allowed.
A backdated transaction dated before the charge-off is not allowed.

tr.td: Charge-off transaction is reversed and replayed; charge-off amount increases or decreases
Charge-off transaction is reprocessed with balances changing

p: You can reverse a charge-off only when the charge-off was applied in error. The reversal removes the charge-off tag from the loan. It is a remediation or exception process, not standard business activity.
Reversal is not supported when:

ul.li: Any transaction exists after the charge-off transaction.
The loan was charged off correctly and the customer later cures or settles the balance.

p: Undoing a charge-off restores the loan to its state before charge-off. You can provide a reverse external id, which is stored on the transaction. The transaction can then be fetched by external id, but not by the reverse external id.
Undo charge-off rules:

ul.li: Undo charge-off does not require any parameter.
Undo charge-off behaves as undo write-off and uses the undo-charge-off command.

p: You can reverse-replay a charge-off transaction to increase or decrease the charge-off amount when a reversal is backdated or a new transaction posts. Reverse-replay for charge-off must be implemented. The charge-off flag is lifted and reapplied only when the charge-off transaction is reprocessed.
Journal entry creation happens immediately when:

ul.li: a new loan transaction is reverse-replayed

p: You cannot reschedule, restructure installments, or add a new charge on a loan account marked as a charge-off. A second charge-off on an already charged-off account returns a validation error, and the same applies to undo charge-off.

The system raises a charge-off event whenever a charge-off happens for a loan account. The event carries an unpaidCharges array listing each unpaid charge group by charge name, with one object per charge name.

tr.td: Sum of transaction.loan.loanCharges.amountOutstanding where the loan charge is unpaid

p: Use the Loan transaction API with the charge-off command to apply a charge-off to a loan. The Loan API also exposes a charged-off flag that indicates whether a loan is charged off.
Charge-off input parameters are:

ul.li: Charge-off date (date field)
Charge-off reason (drop down, optional)
Note (string, optional)
External ID (string, optional)

p: The Charge-off button appears on the Loan details page. The Undo charge-off button appears there only when the loan is already charged-off. Supported fields during charge-off are transactionDate, note, locale, dateFormat, chargeOffReasonId, and externalId. There are no fees or penalties for any charged-off loan, and no validations are added for this on Fineract side.
h2: Accounting JE rules before and after charge-off
p: Transactions after the charge-off date follow charge-off accounting JE rules, while transactions before that date follow pre-charge-off rules.

blockquote.p: Note: The current implementation creates journal entries in bulk at the end of reverse-replay and cannot distinguish pre and post charge-off entries at the moment.

p: Possible strategies for creating journal entries based on the Charge off flag are:

ul.li: Create GL entries one by one per transaction.
Create GL entries in bulk as PRE-Chargeoff and POST-Chargeoff groups.

p: The repayment strategy order decides the sequence in which payments are applied to charge types on a loan. It applies when a payment is allocated after charge-off.
Payments are applied in this order:

In advanced principal
Penalty

Interest

p: Deferred charge-off options are available for non-interest bearing, progressive loan products.

A delinquent loan has a principal balance of 2,000.00 in loans receivable principal (112601) and a fee receivable of 100.00 (112603), giving a total balance of 2,100.00. When the loan is marked as charge-off, the system posts a dummy charge-off transaction for the full balance. The charge-off amount is 2,100.00, is non-editable, and is auto-calculated as the loan balance as of the charge-off date. The loan remains ACTIVE and the portfolio balance does not change; the write-off happens only at the accounting level. The figures in this example are illustrative.
The example shows that charge-off writes off the receivable through accounting entries while the loan stays active and the portfolio balance is unchanged.

If the charge-off was posted in error and no transaction exists after it, the charge-off can be undone. Undoing restores the loan receivable (112601) and fee receivable (112603) and reverses the fee charge-off income. The loan remains ACTIVE throughout and is again treated as a normal active loan for collection. The figures are illustrative.
Undo reverses the accounting write-off and restores the receivables, while the loan remains active and eligible for normal collection.

A payment of 400.00 dated before the charge-off date is posted after the loan has been charged off. Because the transaction date precedes the charge-off, the system reverse-replays the charge-off: it reverses the original charge-off transaction and reposts it using the lower balance as of the charge-off date. The new charge-off amount is 1,700.00, consisting of 1,600.00 principal and 100.00 fee. Interest accrual remains stopped at the charge-off date and does not calculate interest for periods before it.

The example shows that a backdated payment reduces the charge-off amount through reverse-replay, and the loan remains active with accrual stopped at the charge-off date. If the backdated payment fully pays the loan, the charge-off transaction is reversed and the charge-off flag is lifted instead of merely reducing the amount.
See also: Payment Allocation Strategies.
